title: How can a friend know your answer without your number?
description: {{NAME_2}} thinks of a secret number and follows four spoken steps. {{NAME_1}} says the final answer is already known, without hearing the secret number. The video stops on the question of how that can be.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number trick can be explained, and the explanation is the work of this chapter. Collect guesses about why the friend is so sure, and confirm none of them yet.

source: A trick that seems to read your mind
video_script.why: Before any letter appears, the child meets the puzzle that drives the chapter: a trick whose end is known without the start.
video_script.substitution: Picture a secret number in a closed box that goes through four steps the friend calls out.
video_script.anchor: two friends and a secret number that goes through four spoken steps

names.{{NAME_1}}: the friend who sets the number trick and says the final answer in advance
names.{{NAME_2}}: the friend who thinks of the secret number

never_show: any worked try of the trick
the final answer of the trick
maths_rules: The trick has four spoken steps: double the number, add four, divide by two, take away the number first thought of.
The secret number stays a closed box; no starting number is ever chosen or shown.
No numbers or symbols are drawn on screen; the steps appear only as small step cards with pictures.
The open question: how can {{NAME_1}} be sure of the final answer without knowing the start. It is never answered here.
video_script.design: One idea: a trick that seems to read minds asks for a reason. Assumes nothing. The closed box and the four step cards stay to the end of the video.
open_questions: The train compartment photo is a story backdrop from the chapter library; the book itself does not name a setting for the two friends.
